title: Licensing, Frozen Assets, Investigations and Breach Reporting
summary: What firms must do when they hold frozen assets or need a licence, how to investigate a potential breach, and how to report to the authority.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: What firms must do when they hold frozen assets or need a licence, how to investigate a potential breach, and how to report to the authority.
Learning Objectives: Manage frozen assets and reporting obligations correctly
Apply for, rely on and track general and specific licences
Investigate potential breaches and decide on voluntary disclosure
Syllabus: Freezing, holding and reporting frozen funds and economic resources
General and specific licences, wind-down periods and licence conditions
Investigating a potential breach: facts, root cause and remediation
Reporting breaches and suspicions to the authority and the national FIU
Intended Audience: Compliance officers, MLROs, sanctions specialists and financial crime analysts
Payments, operations, trade finance and client onboarding staff who handle screening alerts or transactions
Front-office, relationship and product staff in firms with cross-border clients, payments or trade exposure
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial crime compliance, payments or client onboarding is helpful. No prior specialist sanctions knowledge is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)
Basel Committee, Compliance and the Compliance Function in Banks (2005)
